prompt:
以下はある英語ニュースpodcast記事のFull Story・Point One・Point Twoです。
Point One・Point Twoそれぞれについて、以下6項目を判定してください
(それぞれPASS/FAIL)。

- qa_not_caveat_only: このPointが、研究上の限界・一般化上の注意・免責事項
  だけで構成されていない場合PASS(それらに加えて実質的な新しい内容がある
  場合もPASS。留保だけでPoint枠全体が終わっている場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_full_story_paraphrase: Full Storyの要約・言い換えに留まっていない
  場合PASS(Full Storyの中心的なlogic・結論を語彙だけ変えて繰り返している
  場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_other_point_paraphrase: もう一方のPointの要約・言い換えになって
  いない場合PASS
- qa_explains_why_it_matters: 「だから何なのか」を具体的に説明できている
  場合PASS(聞き手にとっての具体的な意味・示唆がある場合)
- qa_specific_not_generic: この記事のLedger固有の内容に基づいており、他の
  どんな記事にもほぼそのまま流用できる一般論になっていない場合PASS
- qa_adds_new_value: 新しい理解・解釈・意外性・具体的示唆のいずれかを
  実際に加えている場合PASS(Full Storyだけを聞いた場合と比べて、聞き手の
  理解が実際に深まっている場合)

reasoningには、判定理由を1〜2文の日本語で書いてください(特にFAILの場合は
具体的な理由を明記してください)。

【Full Story】
At first, the US-Israel conflict with Iran looked like a war of airstrikes, blockades, and military threats. By September, it is starting to look different: a long economic struggle over whether ships, oil, and energy can move reliably.

The conflict began with US and Israeli airstrikes on Iran on February 28. The United States began its blockade in April. A ceasefire memorandum was agreed on June 14, and the blockade was lifted four days later.

But the pause did not last. After Iran attacked three merchant ships outside approved routes in July, the blockade was restarted on July 14. Since then, pressure has continued at sea and inside Iran’s energy sector.

Reports say an Iranian petrochemical plant stopped production in August. An Iranian opposition media outlet also reported a major loss of natural gas production capacity, although that figure has not been independently confirmed. At the same time, the US Navy found and removed more than 100 objects believed to be mines in a traffic area of the Strait of Hormuz.

The diplomatic path is also narrowing. On August 18, President Trump said no talks with Iran were scheduled. The 60-day period for negotiations then ended without an agreement. One forecast has reportedly moved its expected time for easing tensions from September to the end of the year.

One report now describes the region as returning to a dangerous and increasingly unsustainable military stalemate after about a month of calm.

But the picture is not moving in only one direction. On September 2, Energy Secretary Chris Wright said more than 17 million barrels of oil passed through the strait on September 1, the highest daily level since the war began. That claim suggests Iran may be losing some ability to block the waterway.

The result is a mixed picture: pressure is building, but the evidence does not yet show a clear winner or a clear end to the conflict.

【Point One】
The sharpest disagreement is also a question of time. Wright’s figure may show that some access returned on one day. But official energy data shows that the quarterly average fell from more than 20 million barrels a day before the war to 4.9 million in the second quarter of 2026. A single high day cannot prove a lasting recovery or a permanent loss of Iranian leverage.

【Point Two】
Hormuz is not simply open or closed. The United States reported stopping or checking ships, while one shipping report said that more than 26 ships avoided the blockade. Three merchant ships were attacked outside approved routes, and more than 100 suspected mines were found in a traffic lane. Ships may still move, but uncertain passage can keep the economic pressure in place.

point_one.reasoning: 単日の17百万バレルという数字を、戦前および2026年第2四半期の平均値と比較し、回復が一時的か持続的かを判断する時間軸を加えている。これはFull Storyにない具体的なデータと、イランの影響力を評価する際の実質的な解釈を提供している。

point_two.reasoning: ホルムズ海峡を単純な開閉ではなく、船舶の検査・迂回・攻撃・機雷による不確実な通航状態として整理している。26隻の迂回など具体例を通じて、船が通れる状態でも不確実性が経済的圧力を維持する理由を示しており、Full Storyへの新しい解釈を加えている。
